chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who set out as a pilgrim, and with him was a camel of his, and expense money, and provisions. So he died on the way. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was Sarurah (one who had not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), then died in Ihram, then the Hajj of Al-Islam suffices for him. And if he died while he was Sarurah before he entered into Ihram, his camel and his provisions and his expenses and whatever was with him are made to be for the Hajj of Al-Islam. So if there is something excess from that, then it is for the inheritors, if there are no debts upon him.'

I said, 'What is your view if the Hajj was optional (Nafl), then he died on the way before he entered into Ihram, for whom would be his camel, and his expense money, and whatever was with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'All that was with him and whatever he left would be for the inheritors, except if there are debts upon him, so they are paid off on his behalf; or if he had bequeathed a bequest, so that bequest is executed for the one to whom he bequeathed it, and that is taken from his one-third.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.صَرُورَة: One who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj

ai.seo_question: What happens to a pilgrim's wealth if he dies before or after entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential distinction between dying in the state of Ihram versus before it, determining whether the Hajj obligation is fulfilled or if assets are liquidated for inheritance. It establishes that if the Hajj was obligatory, the pilgrim's wealth covers the cost of a substitute performing Hajj on his behalf, while optional Hajj assets revert fully to heirs after debts and bequests. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the financial continuity of religious duties and the precise allocation of estate assets for posthumous worship.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd Al Ijaly who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about a man who went out as a pilgrim and with him was a camel of his, and expense money, and provisions. So he died on the way’. Heasws said: ‘If he was Saroura (not having had performed Hajj), then died in Ihraam, so it has sufficed from him for Hajj of Al-Islam; but if he died and he was Saroura (not having had performed Hajj) before he wore Ihraam, his camel and his provisions and his expenses would be made to be for a Hajj of Al-Islam. So if there is something excess from that, so it would be for the inheritors, if there do no happen to be debts upon him’.

I said, ‘What is yourasws view if the Hajj was optional, then he died on the way before he wore Ihraam, for whom would be his camel, and his expense money, and whatever was with him?’ Heasws said: ‘Whatever was with him, and whatever he left would happen to be for his inheritors, except if there happen to be debts upon him, so these would be fulfilled on his behalf; or if he had bequeathed with a bequest, so that bequest would be established for the one to whom it had been bequeathed to, and that would be made to be from his one-third (of his wealth/belongings)’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Burayd al-‘Ijliy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who travels for al-Hajj. He has a camel with him and his supplies, but he dies on the way. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it was his first al-Hajj and has died in al-Haram (the sacred area), it is sufficient for Hajjahta al-Islam. If he dies, being his first al- Hajj, before assuming the state of Ihram, his camel, supplies and things with him are applied to his Hajjahta al-Islam, if anything is left extra it is for his heirs, if there is no loan on him.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if it was an optional al-Hajj and he dies on the way before assuming the state of Ihram, who will have his camel, and things with him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘All things belonging to him go to his heirs, unless there is loan on him which is paid on his behalf or if his will says to give something to someone, in which case it is paid from one-third of his legacy.’”
